description: User field. CORRECTS a former CLAUDE.md belief ("A User-type field blocks publish outright") — captured off a REAL, live PUBLISHED builder example (a real production process template, issue #59): a bare Field{Type:"User"} with no sibling QueryDefinition is still the thing that blocks publish; a User field WITH its QueryDefinition{FlowType:"User"} sibling publishes and renders fine. Same Type:"Reference"-family QueryDefinition wiring as field_lookup.json (FlowType "Process") and field_remote_lookup.json (FlowType "Dataset") — User is the third FlowType in that same family, except the FIELD's own Type is "User", not "Reference".
notes: LHSModel on a live User QueryDefinition was observed as BOTH "User" (the plain account-level user directory) and "_employee" (an employee-record source) across 3 live User fields on the same real published flow — both are real, platform-level LHSModel literals, not tenant-specific ones. Which to use depends on which directory the field should resolve against; neither is a default to prefer blindly.

AutoFill:true was present on 2 of the 3 live QueryDefinitions and absent on the 3rd (no AutoFill key at all, not AutoFill:false) — same 'absence is a real state, not a default-false' pattern CLAUDE.md already documents for Textarea AllowFormatting/Attachment CaptureOnly. Set it explicitly only when the field is meant to prefill from a matching Criteria; omit it otherwise, don't assume.

A live QueryDefinition with AutoFill:true also carried its own QueryDefinition::Criteria (the auto-fill MATCH condition — a Criteria/Condition subtree, same family as expression_branch.json's routing conditions, just owned by a QueryDefinition instead of a ProcessDef/Activity). That subtree is NOT captured in this minimal shape — it is optional (the 3rd live example had neither AutoFill nor Criteria and still published/rendered fine) and its own condition literals are always tenant/business-specific, never safe to copy verbatim from one capture into another.

LookupField:[] (empty) on every live example — unlike field_remote_lookup.json's Dataset-backed sibling, a User-type QueryDefinition does not appear to need a populated LookupField list to publish or render.

RUNTIME BINDING ON THIS ENGINE'S OWN DEV TENANT IS STILL UNVERIFIED — this shape proves the WRITE shape publishes and renders on the source production tenant, not that dev has an equivalent user/_employee source to resolve against. Do not upgrade 'publishes clean' to 'usable end to end' without a live dev-tenant item walk through a User field (CLAUDE.md's own THE RULE: a 200/publish proves nothing about runtime behavior).

The bare-Field-blocks-publish caution STILL HOLDS: this shape's whole point is that the QueryDefinition sibling is what makes a User field publishable, not the Field node alone. Never write Type:"User" without also writing its Field::QueryDefinition pair.
